race.name: Low Gap Grasshopper
race.tagline: A dirt-heavy January opener on private Mendocino timber roads.

vitals.field_size: Several hundred riders; exact 2026 count not published
vitals.registration: 2027 registration is open through the organizer's Movemint link; the event page still carries 2026 deadline details
vitals.prize_purse: Cash prizes for top three pro men and women in 2026
vitals.aid_stations: Miles 19 and 42 for the 2026 long course

logistics.explanation: Ukiah is a workable regional base, but the separate staging area and access rules for private Mendocino Redwood Company roads add real race-week friction.

length.explanation: Fifty-nine miles is compact by modern gravel standards, though the climbing density makes the day substantially harder than the number suggests.

technicality.explanation: The route combines fast dirt descents, chunky gravel, and conditions that can turn muddy enough to make tire clearance decisive.

elevation.explanation: The long course packs 6,585 feet into 59 miles, beginning with roughly 1,950 feet of climbing over the opening 13 miles.

climate.explanation: Late January in Mendocino County can deliver cold rain and heavy mud even when temperatures remain moderate.

altitude.explanation: The course stays at low Northern California elevations, so altitude is not a meaningful physiological limiter.

adventure.explanation: Event-only access to private timber roads gives the course a sense of discovery that ordinary public-road gravel events cannot copy.

prestige.explanation: Low Gap opens a Grasshopper series that entered its 29th season in 2026 and is nationally visible inside off-road cycling.

race_quality.explanation: Category starts, chip timing, medical support, stocked aid, bottle drop, event photography, and a full finish party indicate a mature production.

experience.explanation: The private-road setting, hard opening climb, dirt-heavy route, and Todd Grove Park finish make this more distinctive than a standard regional grinder.

community.explanation: The weekend includes a shakeout ride, coffee, a park-based after-party, junior racing, and nonprofit support tied to the NorCal cycling community.

field_depth.explanation: The 2026 start drew riders including Kate Courtney and Peter Stetina, and both elite races were decided against nationally credible fields.

value.explanation: The package is substantial, but the current page no longer publishes a usable entry price for the completed 2026 edition.

expenses.explanation: For Northern California riders this is a drive-to weekend with ordinary Ukiah lodging rather than a destination-flight budget.

cultural_impact.explanation: Low Gap is a recognizable early-season test with national gravel coverage, elite participation, and a long-running series identity.

course_description.character: A climbing-dense, 95-percent dirt long course using roads that are normally closed to public riding.
course_description.signature_challenge: The opening Masonite Road climb gains about 1,950 feet in 13 miles before the race turns into a sequence of fast private-road descents and return climbs.

suffering_zones.label: Masonite Road start
suffering_zones.description: A long opening climb forces an early pacing decision before the dirt sectors have begun.

suffering_zones.label: Sawyer Creek climb
suffering_zones.description: The long course adds roughly 870 feet over 4.5 miles after the first major descent.

suffering_zones.label: Final dirt descent and paved return
suffering_zones.description: Late handling precision and the ability to contribute in a fast group both matter on the run back toward Ukiah.

terrain.surface: 95% dirt and gravel, 5% paved in the official 2026 long course

climate.description: Cool January conditions with meaningful rain and mud risk.

logistics.getting_there: Base in Ukiah and follow the event's staging instructions for Masonite Road; the race does not start directly at packet pickup.
logistics.accommodation: Hotels, motels, and limited camping options are available around Ukiah.
logistics.access_warning: Most of the course crosses private property and may only be ridden during organizer-authorized windows.

history.overview: Low Gap is a long-running opener in the Grasshopper Adventure Series, which held its 29th season in 2026.
notable_moments: The 2026 course changed to a 95-percent dirt long route and added a short-course option.
Alex Wild and Jen Tavé won the 2026 elite races.

final_verdict.one_liner: A short-on-paper, hard-in-practice private-road opener with enough climbing and winter uncertainty to expose lazy preparation.
final_verdict.who_is_it_for: Gravel racers who want dense climbing, fast dirt handling, and a strong Northern California competitive field without committing to an ultra-distance event.
final_verdict.is_it_worth_it: Yes. The organizer has confirmed the January 31, 2027 edition, and the private-road access plus mature Grasshopper production justify the trip for riders prepared for dense climbing and winter dirt.
pro_tips: Train sustained climbing before race season rather than treating this as an easy January opener.
Use tire volume and tread appropriate to the organizer's final mud report, not a midsummer setup.
Practice fueling while climbing because the first hour is too demanding to postpone intake.
